protections: P1: every host-side write/permission operation done as root into a mounted guest filesystem must target a path that, after resolving '..' and guest-image symlinks (resolution done with enough privilege to traverse root-only guest dirs), stays inside the mount root (nova/virt/disk/api.py:314-397).

evidence: nova/virt/disk/api.py:315 os.path.join(fs, path.lstrip('/')) with caller-supplied personality path, no normalisation or containment check
nova/api/openstack/compute/servers.py:501-516 personality path taken verbatim from the request
nova/compute/api.py:152-154 only length of path is checked (quota)
nova/virt/libvirt/driver.py:1428-1431 and :1054-1058 route injected_files to disk.inject_files

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a lexical normpath/'..' check (or os.path.realpath run as the unprivileged nova user) already looks like containment; symlinks inside a user-supplied image are not obviously in scope
evidence: nova/virt/disk/api.py:318 tee runs as root and follows symlinks present in the guest image
etc/nova/rootwrap.d/compute.filters:38-60 no readlink/realpath filter exists, so a root-privileged resolve also needs a rootwrap filter

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the path is a hard-coded constant (root/.ssh/authorized_keys), not user input
evidence: nova/virt/disk/api.py:336-349 mkdir -p, chown root, chmod 700 and tee -a as root on a guest path whose components (root, .ssh, authorized_keys) can be symlinks in the image
nova/virt/disk/api.py:305 reached from inject_data_into_fs whenever key is set; nova/virt/libvirt/driver.py:1347-1348

traps.reason_to_dismiss: fixed path etc/network/interfaces; content is operator-templated network config
evidence: nova/virt/disk/api.py:357-362 mkdir/chown root:root/chmod 755/tee as root through guest-controlled etc and etc/network components
nova/virt/libvirt/driver.py:1384-1387 net only built when a network has injected=True

traps.reason_to_dismiss: fixed filename meta.js at the filesystem root; content is JSON-serialised metadata
evidence: nova/virt/disk/api.py:323-327 tee as root to fs/meta.js which may be a symlink in the image
nova/virt/libvirt/driver.py:1389 metadata comes from instance metadata (user-settable)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: fixed paths etc/passwd and etc/shadow; only active when libvirt_inject_password is enabled; it reads/modifies existing files rather than creating arbitrary ones
evidence: nova/virt/disk/api.py:387-396 root cp from and back to guest etc/passwd and etc/shadow, following image symlinks in both directions
nova/virt/libvirt/driver.py:101 and :1391-1394 gated by libvirt_inject_password

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a check placed on the final file path before tee looks sufficient; mkdir -p 'only creates directories'
evidence: nova/virt/disk/api.py:317 mkdir -p of the parent dir as root runs before any write, so a check placed only at the write step comes after a host-side side effect
nova/virt/disk/api.py:337-339 and :358-360 mkdir/chown/chmod run before tee

traps.reason_to_dismiss: xenapi mounts the image itself and only injects key/net; a fix in inject_data()/inject_files() wrappers looks complete
evidence: nova/virt/xenapi/vm_utils.py:1802-1814 calls disk.inject_data_into_fs on its own tmpdir mount, skipping inject_data()
nova/virt/disk/api.py:299-311 inject_data_into_fs is the documented entry for drivers that mount differently
nova/virt/disk/api.py:315 absolute personality paths ('/etc/foo') are legitimate and are rebased by lstrip('/'); a fix must keep them working
nova/virt/disk/api.py:336, :357 legitimate images may have in-root symlinks (e.g. relative links) that must still resolve inside fs; refusing every symlink or every absolute path over-hardens

masking: B (realpath resolved as the unprivileged nova user cannot traverse root-only guest dirs such as root/.ssh, so symlinks there go unresolved) only shows once A's containment helper exists; at the pinned commit neither exists (nova/virt/disk/api.py:314-397), so a solver that writes A's fix with os.path.realpath reproduces B (unverified against upstream diff)

conflicts.what: refusing all symlinks or all absolute paths to close T2 breaks legitimate absolute personality paths and in-root symlinks in normal images (nova/virt/disk/api.py:315)

resolving with unprivileged os.path.realpath (natural T2 fix) fails to see links inside 0700 guest dirs like root/.ssh, which leaves T3 open; correct fix needs root-side resolution plus a rootwrap filter (etc/nova/rootwrap.d/compute.filters:38-60)

fairness_risks: Absolute personality paths (leading '/') are a normal API use and are rebased by lstrip at nova/virt/disk/api.py:315; a rule that rejects them is wrong.
Guest images legitimately contain symlinks that resolve inside the image root; a rule that refuses any symlink in the path breaks them.

A root-side resolve (readlink -m) needs a new rootwrap filter in etc/nova/rootwrap.d/compute.filters; hidden tests that mock utils.execute must accept either readlink-as-root or an equivalent in-root resolution, otherwise implementation choice is graded rather than behaviour.

design.why: The report points at personality-file traversal (T1, easy anchor). T2 is the mimo-type 'how' trap: the check has to resolve symlinks in the image, and do it with root privilege, not just apply a lexical check. T3 and T6 are deepseek-type: the protection is absent and there is a strong reason to dismiss each one (the path is a hard-coded constant; the password route is behind a config flag). They are separate call sites with different operations (tee -a/chown/chmod vs cp both ways). T7 checks ordering, because mkdir -p runs before any write. T9 should be a must-keep-working test (absolute paths, in-root symlinks), not a counted trap. T4/T5 duplicate T3's reason to dismiss, and T8 is closed for free if the fix goes in the inner helpers.

unverified: Exact content of upstream fixes 2427d4a99bed/b0feaffdb2b1 (A) and ce4b2e27be45/d9577ce9f266 (B) was not read; the description of B as 'realpath run unprivileged and missing symlinks under root-only dirs, fixed by readlink -nm as root' is from advisory knowledge, not this checkout.
Whether A's fix covered metadata, net, key and admin_password call sites (T3-T6 origin published_fix_far_site) is assumed, not verified against the diff.

nova/virt/baremetal/proxy.py:474-477 passes disable_auto_fsck to disk.inject_data, which does not accept it (nova/virt/disk/api.py:230-232); the resulting TypeError is swallowed at proxy.py:479, so the baremetal route looks dead. It is not recorded as a trap.

nova/virt/xenapi/vm_utils.py:1812-1814 passes args shifted (None as metadata, metadata as admin_password) relative to nova/virt/disk/api.py:299; this is a functional bug that affects what T8 exercises.
Whether T7 (mkdir -p creating directories outside the root) would be graded as a security failure on its own depends on the hidden-test design.
